:::{#thm-kraft-converse}
#### Prefix codes exist for lengths that satisfy Kraft's inequality

Let $\ell_1 \le \ell_2 \le \cdots \le \ell_n$
be [positive integer](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/number-systems.html#def-positive-integer)s with

$$\sumto{i}{n} 2^{-\ell_i} \le 1.$$

Then some [prefix code](#def-prefix-code) on $n$ values
has [codeword length](source-coding.qmd#def-code)s $\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_n$.

:::

::: {.proof}

For each $i$, let

$$a_i = \sumof{j < i} 2^{-\ell_j},$$

so that $a_1 = 0$.
Let the codeword $c_i$ be the $\ell_i$ [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit)
that spell $N_i = 2^{\ell_i} a_i$ as a base-2 number,
with zeros added at the front to reach $\ell_i$ digits.

This is possible if $N_i$ is an [integer](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/number-systems.html#def-integers)
with $0 \le N_i < 2^{\ell_i}$.
Each term of $N_i = \sumof{j < i} 2^{\ell_i - \ell_j}$ is an integer,
because $\ell_j \le \ell_i$.
By the assumption,
$a_i + 2^{-\ell_i} \le \sumof{j \le i} 2^{-\ell_j} \le 1$,
so $N_i \le 2^{\ell_i} - 1 < 2^{\ell_i}$.

Suppose that $c_i$ were the beginning of $c_k$ for some $i < k$.
The first $\ell_i$ digits of $c_k$ are the base-2 digits
of the integer part of $N_k / 2^{\ell_k - \ell_i} = 2^{\ell_i} a_k$.
Because $c_i$ is these digits,
this integer part is $N_i$.

But $a_k = a_i + \sumof{i \le j < k} 2^{-\ell_j} \ge a_i + 2^{-\ell_i}$,
so $2^{\ell_i} a_k \ge N_i + 1$,
and the integer part of $2^{\ell_i} a_k$ is at least $N_i + 1$, not $N_i$.
This [contradiction](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-contradiction)
shows that no $c_i$ with $i < k$ begins $c_k$.
Nor can $c_k$ be the beginning of $c_i$ with $i < k$:
that would give $\ell_k \le \ell_i$,
so $\ell_k = \ell_i$ and $c_k = c_i$,
which the first case excludes.

:::
